title: Some tools return error messages in Claude Desktop
body: I used mcp-unity with Claude Desktop. When Claude used the select_gameobject or execute_menu_item tools, they were executed correctly in the Unity editor, but the message returned to Claude Desktop as a result of using the tools was "Unsupported content type: undefined". Claude judges that this tool is not working properly. On the other hand, the notify_message tool returns the message "Message displayed:" correctly. I looked at the source a little, and noticed that in the Unity extension, notify_message returns a json containing "type", while select_gameobject and execute_menu_item do not contain a "type". And I think the error is occurring because the websocket server code is trying to access a non-existent "type". Sorry if I'm mistaken.

title: README Suggestion: Unity *needs to be* in focus or tools may time out
body:
According to my testing (Mac / Apple Silicon), essentially all of the tools rely on the Unity window being in focus to execute, potentially because its main thread heavily throttles function calls if the application is not in focus. In other words, you might see the tool requests time out UNLESS you switch back to Unity to let them execute.

Marking "Run in Background" seems to only affect builds, as far as I can tell, and doesn't help.  

There may be a way around this, but for now, everyone using this should know this limitation.

title: No Meta File
body:
Asset Packages/com.gamelovers.mcp-unity/Server/build/log.txt has no meta file, but it's in an immutable folder. The asset will be ignored.

Asset Packages/com.gamelovers.mcp-unity/Server/node_modules has no meta file, but it's in an immutable folder. The asset will be ignored.

There are a lot of these errors in Unity. Everything seems to be connected ok. Using Unity 2022.3.60f1 and Claude Desktop. 

From Claude:
Those warnings are occurring because Unity is detecting assets in the MCP Unity package that don't have corresponding .meta files. Meta files are Unity's way of tracking assets, and when they're missing for assets in packages, Unity typically ignores those assets rather than generating new meta files (since package folders are considered "immutable").
In this case:

"log.txt" in the Server/build directory
The entire "node_modules" folder in the Server directory

These warnings aren't necessarily critical errors that will prevent the MCP Unity server from working, but they indicate that:

The package author didn't properly include meta files for all assets
Some server-side Node.js components may not be properly integrated with Unity

To address these warnings:

You can safely ignore them if the MCP server is still functioning properly
If you're experiencing issues with the server, you might need to contact the package author (CoderGamester) to provide a fixed version with proper meta files

The fact that the "node_modules" folder is being flagged suggests this package includes a Node.js application as part of its server implementation, which might explain some of the communication issues you're experiencing.

title: [Bug] MCP Unity menu item not visible
body: Since the package lacks an assembly, Unity excludes it from compilation, so the MCP Unity button doesn’t appear in the editor tools menu. This will happen in any project that uses assemblies and just adding an editor assembly in MCP Unity Server/Editor will solve it.
